item.title: Self hosted
item.description:
Container Usage

The application can run without copying config.yaml into the container. If no config file exists, it will automatically create one with sensible defaults.

item.title: Configuration
item.description:
The config.yaml file contains all application settings. Key sections:

  • libraryPath / downloadPath: Where the library lives and where downloads land
  • import: Import settings and file organization rules (see Importing and Paths)
  • metadata: Metadata provider settings (musicbrainz, deezer, discogs, acoustid)
  • lyrics: Lyrics provider settings (see Lyrics)
  • downloaders: External service configurations in the form of plugins. Supports both local .so files and automatic building from Git repositories (see Downloading)
  • jobs: Job logs and webhooks (see Jobs)
  • server, database, logger: Web server port, SQLite path and logging
  • telegram: Bot configuration and allowed users (deprecated, will be removed in v0.30.0)

Security Note: Never commit sensitive values like tokens or API keys to version control. Use environment variables or secret files instead.

item.title: Paths
item.description: Path templates decide where each track is placed in your library folder, based on its tags. This page describes the placeholders and functions you can use in them. Templates are used both when importing and when reorganizing your library.

item.title: Importing
item.description: Soulsolid imports music from folders on the server. When importing, it reads each file’s tags, checks whether you already have the song, moves or copies the file into your library folder, and creates artists and albums as needed.

item.title: Downloading
item.description: Soulsolid can download music from online music services through downloader plugins. Soulsolid itself isn’t tied to any service: each service is supported by its own plugin, which you add to your configuration. Anyone can write a plugin for a new service (see the Plugin Development Guide).

item.title: Plugins
item.description: This guide is for developers who want to write a downloader plugin for Soulsolid in Go. If you just want to use an existing plugin, see Downloading instead; no code needed.

item.title: Analyze
item.description:
The analyze feature runs an analysis of the metadata of your library and fills in the missing gaps.

Analyze Jobs

Each analysis runs as a background job and can be started from the Analyze section of the web UI.

item.title: Lyrics
item.description: Soulsolid can find lyrics for your tracks and embed them in the audio files, using lyrics providers. Lyrics providers are separate from downloader plugins, so you get lyrics no matter where your music came from.

item.title: Jobs
item.description: Long-running tasks like imports, downloads and analyses run in the background as jobs. The jobs section configures their log files and webhooks. Jobs themselves are kept in memory (the list is emptied on restart), while their logs are saved as files, by default in ./logs/jobs.
